title: Removing Timing Shortcuts Improves Non-Invasive Brain-to-Text
abstract: arXiv:2609.40359v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We find that major reported improvements in decoding words from non-invasive brain recordings are largely reproducible without any brain data. In the influential work of d'Ascoli et al. (2025), time series of brain activity from subjects perceiving continuous speech are segmented into fixed-length windows starting at each word. A neural network then generates predictions for all of the words in a sentence together. Neighbouring windows partially overlap, implicitly revealing the interval between words. Since these intervals indicate the duration of the words spoken, and different words tend to have different durations - for example, "the" is much shorter than "supercalifragilisticexpialidocious" - the neural network can improve its predictions of words without relying on the underlying brain activity. Consistent with this, the method reaches 22.0% balanced accuracy on synthetic signals containing no brain information, compared with 22.3%

translated_title: 移除时间捷径可提升无创脑-文本解码技术
translated_abstract: 我们发现，从无创大脑记录中解码单词所报告的主要改进，在很大程度上可以在完全不含大脑数据的情况下复现。在d'Ascoli等人（2025年）颇具影响力的工作中，来自正在聆听连续语音的受试者的大脑活动时间序列被分割成以每个单词为起点的固定长度窗口，随后由神经网络一次性生成对句子中所有单词的预测。由于相邻窗口部分重叠，隐式地揭示了单词之间的时间间隔，而这些间隔指示了所读单词的时长——不同单词往往具有不同的时长，例如"the"远短于"supercalifragilisticexpialidocious"——神经网络无需依赖底层大脑活动即可改进其对单词的预测。与此一致，该方法在不含任何大脑信息的合成信号上达到了22.0%的平衡准确率，相比之下（真实大脑数据上）为22.3%。
tldr: 无创脑-文本解码的主要性能提升源于窗口重叠隐式泄露的时间捷径——不含任何大脑数据也能取得近乎相同的成绩，而移除这些时间捷径才能真正提升解码性能。
en_tdlr: Reported gains in non-invasive brain-to-text decoding largely stem from timing shortcuts leaked by overlapping window segmentation and are reproducible without any brain data; removing these shortcuts improves decoding.
